parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The three files cover one concern: request contracts (create, update, search) for the email-template feature. They also use one abstraction consistently: class-validator decorators combined with @nestjs/swagger PartialType.

The field rules (title length and uniqueness, sender email, body minimum length) live once, in CreateEmailTemplateDto. UpdateEmailTemplateDto gets those rules through PartialType(CreateEmailTemplateDto) rather than copying them. EmailTemplatesSearchFilterDto reuses the shared CommonSearchFieldDto through PartialType instead of defining its own search fields.

The one weak spot is in UpdateEmailTemplateDto: it declares `title` again with @ApiPropertyOptional, @Optional and @IsString. @Optional comes from @nestjs/common and is a dependency-injection decorator, not a validation one. @IsString repeats a rule that the class already gets from CreateEmailTemplateDto. This override is redundant and slightly misleading, but it doesn't create a second, conflicting home for a rule. It doesn't skip the module's abstractions either, since PartialType is still used. I'm treating it as a minor quality note, not as a split concern or a duplicated rule that would fail the unit.
